meta.name: Public-Safe Proofs Bank
meta.purpose: Repo-internal source-of-truth claim graph for Jamie Burkart's professional accomplishments. The website projects from this graph with audience, purpose, and care.
meta.publicationRule: This repository is public. Do not include anything here that would create harm, breach trust, or require apology if printed in a newspaper.

postures.label: Known
postures.definition: Public-safe and evidence-backed enough to say directly in website copy.

postures.label: Open
postures.definition: Potentially useful but requires approval, stronger citation, screenshot review, collaborator confirmation, or tighter wording before publication.

postures.label: Protected
postures.definition: Intentionally omitted because privacy, consent, client trust, law, civic sensitivity, or community safety requires it.

coreClaim.claim: Jamie Burkart is a technical project manager and product operations / implementation lead who builds operating structure for complex public-facing teams.
boundaries: Do not imply sole authorship of collective civic wins.
Do not publish private archives as proof.
Prefer source-backed role language over inflated outcome claims.

entities.name: NYC Artist Coalition
entities.roleClaim: Jamie is a co-founder and civic-systems / documentation / policy-communications lead for NYC Artist Coalition.
entities.evidenceSummary: Public campaign history supports collective work around Cabaret Law repeal advocacy, Office of Nightlife / SaveNYCSpaces advocacy, M.A.R.C.H. transparency work, and Fair Rent NYC / Commercial Rent Stabilization advocacy.
entities.websiteProjection: Use as coalition infrastructure: campaign sites, explainers, testimony support, source maps, meeting memory, action materials, and public-safe language.
boundaries: Do not claim Jamie alone passed laws, created offices, wrote legal analysis, or owned the movement.
Do not publish private coalition notes, stakeholder lists, or strategy records.

entities.name: Harry J. Epstein Company
entities.roleClaim: Jamie helped an 80+ year-old industrial business translate paper-and-phone catalog operations into searchable e-commerce, analytics, publishing, product-data, and workflow systems.
entities.evidenceSummary: Public and archival sources support the online-store launch and public features. Resume/source materials support Jamie's implementation role and contribution language around a period of 2x revenue growth.
entities.websiteProjection: Use as private-sector technical project management, e-commerce operations, analytics, content, and workflow proof.
boundaries: No private dashboards, customer data, revenue detail, vendor terms, credentials, or internal operating documents.
Use contribution language for business outcomes.

entities.name: FairRentNYC / Commercial Rent Stabilization
entities.roleClaim: Jamie helped build and steward public-safe campaign-memory and coordination infrastructure for Commercial Rent Stabilization and storefront-stability advocacy.
entities.evidenceSummary: Public-safe records support 30+ pages of running minutes, action trackers, source maps, legal/policy question logs, public-data framing, consent-aware story handling, and follow-up protocols.
entities.websiteProjection: Use as civic operations, documentation architecture, public/private boundary, and source-backed memory proof.
boundaries: No private coalition notes, legal-review materials, stakeholder lists, raw strategy documents, private emails, unapproved quotes, or sensitive tenant/business details.
Use policy-neutral language when describing public-data opportunities.

entities.name: CallNYC
entities.roleClaim: Jamie built an archived civic-data prototype translating newly released City Council constituent-services open data into resident-facing find-help / next-steps guidance.
entities.evidenceSummary: Archive traces include press/civic-tech references, a public GitHub trace, and CouncilStat release / hackathon context.
entities.websiteProjection: Use as open-data translation, resident-facing civic interface, scope-disclaimer, and public-prototype proof.
boundaries: Do not imply current public-service status, official City Council affiliation, legal guidance, or emergency-service guidance.

entities.name: WOWList
entities.roleClaim: Jamie designed and co-built a Python / Django, PostgreSQL / PostGIS, and Ember.js community-calendar and social discovery platform organized around followable keyword communities.
entities.evidenceSummary: Local aggregate archive analysis shows 1,846 users, 16,142 posts/events, 23,864 lists/tags, 28,837 list follows, 20,927 saved/starred events, 15,915 synced Google Calendar events, and 35+ active city scenes by July 2017.
entities.websiteProjection: Use as full-stack public platform, social product logic, community publishing, event distribution, and product-operations proof.
boundaries: Do not publish raw user data, emails, contact lists, password/session data, private media, or user-level examples without approval.

entities.name: Sunday Dinner / 196 Artists Residency
entities.roleClaim: Jamie created repeatable hosting, onboarding, facilitation, documentation, and continuity systems across 300+ gatherings and 20+ resident artists.
entities.evidenceSummary: Private aggregate records show numbered gatherings through 345 and substantial participation infrastructure.
entities.websiteProjection: Use as onboarding, facilitation, hospitality systems, artist support, continuity, and consent-boundary proof.
boundaries: No guest lists, attendance records, addresses, phone numbers, private stories, private scores, or unapproved photos.

entities.name: Source-Backed Team Memory
entities.roleClaim: Jamie is developing a bounded lab method for source-backed team memory: reviewable, human-correctable, source-linked operating memory for knowledge-heavy teams.
entities.evidenceSummary: Public-safe lab materials support Known / Open / Protected, decision records, source inventories, transcript-to-minutes workflows, governance policies, eval ideas, human review, and Markdown-first knowledge pages.
entities.websiteProjection: Use as a lab / proof-of-practice connecting technical project management, product operations, documentation architecture, AI eval discipline, human review, and governance.
boundaries: Not a finished SaaS, chatbot, private archive browser, surveillance system, legal/medical advice system, or replacement for human judgment.

projectionRules: The website should read as a composed portfolio, not a claims database.
Use this graph to choose strong, audience-relevant claims, then write them in human language.
Keep protected details out of both the website and this public repository.
When a claim is open, either omit it or mark it as a launch blocker outside public-facing copy.
